native_result.query: How does the consideration of academic characteristics alter the effects of Socioeconomic Status and race on BA degree completion?
native_result.HypoA: When academic characteristics are considered, the effect of SES on BA degree completion is reduced and the effect of race is enlarged.
native_result.HypoB: Academic characteristics (ASVAB achievement and class rank) account for a large share — roughly 30-60% — of the positive SES gradient in college attendance/completion proxied by dormitory residence, and essentially all of the small negative gradient for the Black-coded cohort (coefficient attenuates ~70-96% to ≈0); the Hispanic-coded cohort's positive gradient is not attenuated but amplified after academic controls. SES effects operate largely through measured academic ability. Because the file contains no direct BA-completion indicator, all statements concern attendance/completion proxied by ever living in a dorm/fraternity/sorority (NLSY79 residence code 3, any wave 1981-1996; sensitivity: 1985+ only).
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded data/nls_raw.csv (12,686 x 61). Constructed outcomes: ever-dorm any wave 1981-96 (NLSY residence code 3) and sensitivity ever-dorm 1985+ waves. SES block: mother's grade, father's grade, ln(1+family income 1979), family size 1979. Race: cohort1/cohort2 indicators vs cohort3 reference. Covariates: sex, age. Academic block: four ASVAB scores re-standardized (raw values arrived on 165-825 scale despite 'Z Score' labels) + class-rank percentile (1 - rank/class size). Nested logistic regressions (statsmodels Logit): Model 1 SES+race baseline vs Model 2 + academic controls; complete-case primary (N=3,760), ASVAB-only (N=7,593), rank-only (N=4,041), and median-imputation + collapsed missing-indicator robustness (N=8,563). Reported log-odds, odds ratios, and % attenuation; % flagged unstable where |M1 log-odds|<0.05. Group means by racial/ethnic cohort reported for label sanity-checking. All 10 fits converged; post-1985 wealth/income excluded as post-treatment.
